blocks.text: This page tracks the Cloverdale MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for October 2026: $930,600 for a typical home, down 4.6% over twelve months.
Cloverdale benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical Cloverdale home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $930,600 in October 2026. That is little changed at +0.9% on the month, little changed at −1.1% over three months, down 3.0% over six months and down 4.6% over the year. Over three years it is down 9.6%, and over five years down 6.4%.
The weakest one-year move in Cloverdale was for an apartment homes at −8.9%; the strongest was a townhouse at −4.4%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,326,400) and an apartment ($501,800) is $824,600, and a townhouse ($757,900) sits $256,100 above the apartment benchmark.
Against the Fraser Valley Board area, where the all-home benchmark was $860,000, Cloverdale is 8.2% above. Over the year the Fraser Valley Board area moved down 6.4% against down 4.6% here.
Of the 8 areas this board reports, Cloverdale ranks 4 by all-home benchmark, with Langley above it at $932,900 and Surrey below it at $899,900.

Detached homes in Cloverdale: benchmark $1,326,400, little changed at +0.7% in a month, down 2.1% in three months, down 4.0% in six months, down 6.0% in a year, down 8.6% in three years and down 7.9% in five. That is 2.5% above the detached benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($1,293,800).

Townhouse homes in Cloverdale: benchmark $757,900, little changed at +0.5% in a month, little changed at −0.6% in three months, down 2.0% in six months, down 4.4% in a year, down 10.5% in three years and down 2.5% in five. That is 2.1% above the townhouse benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($742,300).

Apartment homes in Cloverdale: benchmark $501,800, little changed at −1.0% in a month, little changed at −1.0% in three months, down 6.8% in six months, down 8.9% in a year, down 12.5% in three years and down 3.9% in five. That is 8.9% above the apartment benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($460,800).

blocks.text: Set against October 2025, Cloverdale had 31 detached sales (33 a year earlier), 25 townhouse sales (33 a year earlier) and 3 apartment sales (15 a year earlier). Month-end active listings were 191 detached (about 200 a year earlier), 138 townhouse (about 141 a year earlier) and 68 apartment (about 93 a year earlier). Dividing sales by active listings gives a sales-to-active ratio of 16.2% for detached, 18.1% for townhouse and 4.4% for apartment.

In dollars, the typical Cloverdale home is worth about $44,900 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $975,500. By type, detached homes lost about $84,700, from $1,411,100 to $1,326,400, townhouses lost about $34,900, from $792,800 to $757,900, and apartments lost about $49,000, from $550,800 to $501,800 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $959,400 six months ago and near $1,029,400 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $28,800 below the six-month mark and about $98,800 below the three-year mark. Against the Fraser Valley Board area, the Cloverdale benchmark is about $70,600 above the regional $860,000; a year earlier the difference was about $56,700 above.
Cloverdale sales at a glance, past 12 months

Over the past year, 345 Cloverdale houses sold at a median of $1.29M (middle half $1.15M to $1.45M), half of them within 21 days. 133 condos sold at a median of $465,000 (middle half $410,000 to $562,500), half within 28 days. Quarter by quarter, the median house price eased from $1.38M to $1.24M between November–January and August–October (60 and 76 sales).

blocks.text: What the Cloverdale figure is
The $930,600 Cloverdale figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Fraser Valley Real Estate Board for October 2026.
